title: Retrospective analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron strains (2023 to 2024) from Pakistan reveals differential phylogenetic diversity across genomes compared with other countries

analysis.research_question_and_background: SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants continued to emerge globally in 2023 and 2024 however, genomic epidemiology from Pakistan has been limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We compared Omicron variants in Pakistan by studying phylogenetic diversity and entropy across genomes compared with isolates from Western countries USA, UK and France, as well as neighbouring India.
analysis.methods: We studied SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected between January 2023 and September 2024. For Pakistan, we also focused on RT-PCR positive samples from Aga Khan University Hospital. Statistical analyses identified P value < 0.05 as considered significant. Genome-based lineages were assigned using Pangolin v4.4 pangoLEARN with clade assignment using Nextclade v3.5.0. Sequences were aligned using MAFFT v7.505 and a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree was constructed with IQ-TREE v2.2.0. Substitution rates and Shannon genomic entropy was determined.
analysis.main_results: In Pakistan, XBB.1 and its subvariants were predominant in 2023 and JN.1 and its subvariants persisted through 2024. Whilst, variants KP.2, LB.1, and LA.1 emerging by mid-2024, JN.1 remained dominant. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 in US, UK and France showed XBB.1.5 transitioned to JN.1 and KP.3.3 by September 2024. Notably, JN.1 strains persisted in India until 2024. Genomic substitution rates in Pakistan at 0.467E-04 (95CI: 3.29E-04-6.04E-04) were similar compared with those from USA, UK and France, but higher than those from India. SARS-CoV-2 mean positional entropy in Pakistan at 0.0324 was higher (other countries 0.01-0.013).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We describe Omicron diversity in Pakistan with persistence of XBB and JN.1 lineage strains into 2024. These finding provide insights into SARS-CoV-2 genomic evolution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Expanded surveillance is required to understand local transmission of pandemic strains.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The relatively small genomic sequences available limits the comparison with substitution rates between global strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a retrospective analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron strains in Pakistan from 2023 to 2024, comparing their phylogenetic diversity and genomic entropy with those from the USA, UK, France and India. The research identified XBB.1 and JN.1 as predominant in Pakistan, with JN.1 remaining dominant through 2024. In contrast, the USA, UK and France showed a transition from XBB.1.5 to JN.1 and KP.3.3 by September 2024, while JN.1 persisted in India until 2024. Genomic substitution rates in Pakistan were similar to those in Western countries but higher than in India. The mean positional entropy in Pakistan was also higher than in other countries. The study highlights the need for expanded surveillance to understand local transmission dynamics of pandemic strains. However, the relatively small number of genomic sequences limits the strength of the comparison with global strains.

title: A monoclonal antibody panel to track antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 JN.1 subvariants

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to address the ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2, where many existing monoclonal antibodies have lost activity against recent variants, limiting their ability to resolve the antigenic effects of mutations arising in emerging lineages.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved generating a mAb panel by immunizing naive, unimprinted VelocImmune mice with the KP.3.1.1 spike, and isolating and characterizing 11 human neutralizing antibodies targeting diverse epitopes of evolved variants.
analysis.methods: The methods included immunizing mice with the KP.3.1.1 spike, isolating and characterizing 11 human neutralizing antibodies, and integrating these antibodies with characterized mAbs to establish a toolbox for profiling antigenic evolution among emerging variants.
analysis.main_results: The panel was applied to emerging variants, providing mechanistic insight into recent antigenic evolution, highlighting the potential role of altered receptor-binding domain conformation, and revealing clear differences in antibody-evasion profiles between JN.1-derived lineages and BA.3.2 lineages.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings established an updated mAb panel for monitoring antigenic evolution of JN.1 subvariants, offering new insights into the antigenic effects of mutations in emerging variants.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 variants, aiding in the development of more effective treatments and vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of a specific mAb panel and the focus on JN.1 subvariants, which may not generalize to other variants. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited scope of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study generated a mAb panel to track the antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 JN.1 subvariants, revealing differences in antibody-evasion profiles between JN.1 and BA.3.2 lineages. The findings provide new insights into the antigenic effects of mutations and establish an updated panel for monitoring variant evolution.

title: Structural and functional analysis of VYD222: A broadly neutralizing antibody against SARS-CoV-2 variants.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the issue of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies becoming ineffective due to extensive mutations in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. The research sought to demonstrate the improved neutralization potency and breadth of VYD222 (pemivibart) against SARS-CoV-2 variants despite substantial virus evolution.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved structural and functional analysis of VYD222, a human mAb re-engineered from ADG20 (adintrevimab), to assess its neutralization potency and breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the recently dominant XFG variant.
analysis.methods: VYD222 was analyzed using X-ray crystal structures to understand its interaction with the receptor-binding domains of SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron BA.5. Deep mutational scanning was employed to evaluate the escape-resistant neutralization of VYD222 against a broad panel of clinically relevant SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.main_results: VYD222 demonstrated potent neutralization against a broad range of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the XFG variant. Structural analysis revealed that VYD222 accommodates mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants that escape other FDA-approved antibodies, particularly those occurring in the second shell outside the paratope contact residues.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide crucial insights into the escape-resistant neutralization of VYD222 against a broad panel of clinically relevant SARS-CoV-2 variants, offering valuable guidance for risk assessment of emergent variants.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results are significant for surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly for immunocompromised individuals. The structural and functional analysis of VYD222 can inform the development of more robust therapeutic strategies against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of X-ray crystal structures and deep mutational scanning, which may not fully capture the dynamic nature of viral evolution. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on structural and computational methods without direct in vivo validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed VYD222, a re-engineered monoclonal antibody, to demonstrate its improved neutralization potency against SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the XFG variant. Structural and functional analysis provided insights into how VYD222 accommodates mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants, offering valuable guidance for risk assessment and therapeutic development.

title: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].

analysis.scope_and_question: The review analyzes the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state, and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents during the transition from the acute phase to adaptation of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021 compared with 2020.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts, and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the decrease in adherence to preventive measures and the polarization of vaccination attitudes. However, the methods used may have limitations, and the data do not fully address the reasons behind these changes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups, and horizontal trust.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzed the dynamics of preventive behavior and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents during the transition from the acute phase to adaptation of the COVID-19 pandemic. By the 5th wave, adherence to preventive measures decreased, and vaccination attitudes became more polarized.

title: Echoes of infection: viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes in long COVID: a systematic review

analysis.scope_and_question: Long COVID, or post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC), affects an estimated 10–20% of individuals following SARS-CoV-2 infection. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes across multiple organ systems, drawing from studies of individuals with Long COVID as well as broader post-acute cohorts, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports relevant to Long COVID pathophysiology.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Following PRISMA guidelines and holding a PROSPERO registration (CRD420261403869), a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible reports were stratified as (A) symptom-defined Long COVID assessed at or after 12 weeks, (B) post-acute or mixed populations without a consistently confirmed Long COVID definition or timing, (C) autopsy studies, and (D) isolated case/fetal reports. Findings were synthesized narratively by specimen, assay target, and unit of analysis. JBI checklists were used for item-level appraisal, not as certainty-of-evidence ratings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review supports biological heterogeneity after SARS-CoV-2 infection, including residual viral material, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair. SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA, viral proteins, and markers compatible with recent viral activity were reported in selected tissue and blood compartments, but detection varied with population selection, timing, specimen, and assay.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: No included study established replication competence by recovery of infectious virus. Histopathological abnormalities included inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and vascular injury; however, causal attribution to Long COVID was limited by acute disease severity, biopsy indication, comorbidity, and incomplete comparator data. A single participant total was not reported because of overlapping cohorts, repeated sampling, and outcome-specific denominators.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Organ-specific prevalence, a hierarchy of tissue tropism, replication-competent reservoirs, and superiority of antiviral or immunomodulatory treatment remain undefined. Standardized Long COVID definitions, representative cohorts, validated assays, appropriate comparators, and longitudinal studies linking biological markers to clinical outcomes are required.

title: A dose of reality: autodisable syringe supply challenges in the COVID-19 immunization response.

analysis.scope_and_question: Autodisable (AD) syringes are vital for safe immunization, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, as they prevent reuse and reduce the risk of disease transmission.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, global supply was stable and met routine immunization needs. The rapid rollout of COVID-19 vaccines led to a surge in demand for AD syringes, including those with nonstandard dose volumes, which required new product development and matching of syringes to specific vaccines-a synchronization that is typically not needed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pandemic, however, highlighted coordination challenges in aligning vaccine and injection device supply chains. Although manufacturing capacity expanded, syringe shortages still emerged, increasing the risk of dosing errors and placing additional strain on health systems.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Limited early information on COVID-19 vaccine dose volume specifications, long lead times, and lack of coordination between vaccine and syringe stakeholders created forecasting difficulties.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: As demand later declined, oversupply and market instability followed, prompting contract adjustments. This paper incorporates lessons learned from the COVID-19 response and emphasizes that syringes must not be an afterthought in immunization planning for both future outbreak preparedness and routine immunization efforts.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the challenges of supplying autodisable (AD) syringes during the COVID-19 immunization response. It highlights the critical role of AD syringes in preventing reuse and reducing disease transmission, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The review notes that prior to the pandemic, global supply of AD syringes was stable and met routine immunization needs. However, the rapid rollout of vaccines created a surge in demand for AD syringes with nonstandard dose volumes, requiring new product development and synchronization between vaccines and syringes. Despite expanded manufacturing capacity, syringe shortages emerged, increasing the risk of dosing errors and straining health systems. The review also discusses the difficulties in forecasting due to limited early information on vaccine dose specifications and lack of coordination between stakeholders. It concludes that syringes must be a central consideration in immunization planning, both for outbreak preparedness and routine efforts, and outlines strategies to strengthen syringe market resilience.

title: Modelling severe COVID-19 by adaptation of SARS-CoV-2 in Syrian hamsters.

analysis.research_question_and_background: While most patients infected with recent Omicron subvariants develop milder disease than those infected with preceding SARS-CoV-2 strains, some patients remain susceptible to developing severe disease and/or long-term complications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The pathogenesis of and optimal countermeasures for severe COVID-19 remain incompletely understood. Readily available small animal models closely mimicking severe COVID-19 are lacking.
analysis.methods: In this study, we established a new Syrian hamster model resembling severe COVID-19 using a hamster-adapted SARS-CoV-2 (SARS-CoV-2HA) obtained through serial passage.
analysis.main_results: Compared to the ancestral virus strain P0, SARS-CoV-2HA P16 causes more severe disease with significantly higher clinical scores, higher viral burden, more weight loss, prominent cytokine storm, and significant pulmonary injury.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Using this new SARS-CoV-2HA P16 model, we showed that nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir were effective in improving the clinical and virological parameters of hamsters with severe COVID-19.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This new model serves as a robust platform for investigating the pathogenesis of and countermeasures for severe COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Age and sex are key factors influencing disease severity in this model.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a Syrian hamster model that closely mimics severe COVID-19, addressing the lack of such models. The researchers adapted SARS-CoV-2 through serial passage to create a strain (SARS-CoV-2HA P16) that induced more severe disease in hamsters compared to the ancestral strain P0, as evidenced by higher clinical scores, viral burden, weight loss, cytokine storm, and pulmonary injury. The model demonstrated the effectiveness of nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir in improving clinical and virological outcomes in severe cases. The study highlights the importance of age and sex in disease severity and provides a valuable platform for further research on severe COVID-19 pathogenesis and countermeasures. However, the findings are limited to the hamster model and may not fully translate to human conditions.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on SARS-CoV-2 and evaluates the relationship between the target residence time of four Mpro inhibitors and their antiviral activity. analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of the pharmacokinetic properties of Mpro inhibitors. analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study concludes that the residence time of Mpro inhibitors in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells is associated with their antiviral activity. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence highlights a potential limitation in early drug discovery methods, which primarily used non-cell-based assays. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that future drug development should prioritize compounds with longer target residence times to enhance antiviral efficacy. The evidence underscores the importance of residence time in determining drug effectiveness and highlights the need for more in vivo studies to assess performance against emerging variants. The findings suggest that future drug development should focus on improving residence time to optimize antiviral activity and dosing strategies.

title: SARS-CoV-2 antibody landscape following multiple vaccinations and infections during Omicron period

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the effects of repeated COVID-19 vaccination on antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 variants, addressing the incompletely understood immunogenicity, breadth, and durability of these responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study included participants from a prospective cohort in Michigan who had received at least five COVID-19 vaccine doses between 2020 and 2025.
analysis.methods: Serum IgG, IgM, and ACE2 percent inhibition were measured using multiplex assays, and baseline-adjusted immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and formulation-specific antibody durability were evaluated using regression models.
analysis.main_results: Twenty-one participants were included, with higher baseline immunity associated with smaller post-vaccination increases in antibody levels. Antibody landscapes demonstrated broad cross-reactivity against ancestral and Omicron variants, with formulation-specific differences in durability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Repeated vaccination maintained baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses, with formulation-specific differences in durability, suggesting that repeated boosting continues to reinforce humoral immunity despite increasingly complex immune histories.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that despite waning, antibody levels generally remained relatively high across variants up to 300 days post-vaccination, with formulation-specific differences in durability, which can inform vaccine strategies and public health policies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its prospective cohort design and the sample size, which may not be generalizable to the broader population. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of repeated COVID-19 vaccination on antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 variants, showing that baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses were maintained, with formulation-specific differences in durability.

title: Misperceived norms and willingness to get a COVID-19 vaccine: a whole-population study of adults in rural Uganda.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the impact of perceived social norms on vaccine uptake in a rural Ugandan population, addressing a knowledge gap in HIV-endemic settings regarding perceptions about others' willingness to get vaccinated for COVID-19.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among all adults in 8 villages in Uganda from 2021 to 2022, with a 90% response rate.
analysis.methods: Participants completed a survey assessing their personal willingness to get a COVID-19 vaccine, their perceptions of others' willingness, and related beliefs. A multivariable Poisson regression model was used to estimate associations between perceptions and personal willingness.
analysis.main_results: Among 1561 participants, 75% were willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine. Misperceptions about others' willingness to get vaccinated were common, with one in three vaccine-hesitant participants and one in ten vaccine-willing participants incorrectly believing that fewer than half of their village would get vaccinated. Those with such misperceptions were less likely to report personal willingness to get vaccinated.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that misperceptions about others' vaccine uptake significantly influenced personal willingness, suggesting that providing accurate information about vaccine effectiveness and communicating that most adults are willing to get vaccinated could increase uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of addressing misperceptions about vaccine uptake to foster conversations about accessing vaccines and reduce vaccine-related stigma, particularly in HIV-endemic settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the findings may not be generalizable to other populations. The sample was from a specific rural Ugandan setting, which may limit external validity.

analysis.summary_en: This study in rural Uganda found that misperceptions about others' willingness to get a COVID-19 vaccine significantly influenced personal willingness. Providing accurate information could increase vaccine uptake.

title: A decoupled ensemble framework for real-time nowcasting of COVID-19 case numbers and transmission dynamics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitation of right-censoring bias in real-time estimation of the time-varying effective reproductive number (Rt) from case data, which is essential for guiding public health and social measures during SARS-CoV-2 transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed and evaluated a three-step framework for decoupling case forecasting from Rt estimation using daily PCR-confirmed case counts from Hong Kong's Omicron outbreaks (February to December 2022).
analysis.methods: Daily PCR-confirmed case counts were forecast up to 14 days ahead using an ensemble of 10 statistical, machine learning, and deep learning models. Forecasted cases were then deconvolved to reconstruct infection timelines, from which Rt was estimated for up to 7 days ahead.
analysis.main_results: An unweighted ensemble of top-performing models substantially improved forecast accuracy, reducing the root mean square error and the mean absolute percentage error by 10 and 9% for case numbers and by 38 and 34% for Rt.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This approach mitigates right-censoring artefacts by generating Rt estimates from projected rather than truncated case data, enabling accurate real-time monitoring of epidemic burden and transmission dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The framework supports timely public health decision-making by providing accurate real-time monitoring of epidemic burden and transmission dynamics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the need for additional data to stabilize Rt estimates and the potential for bias in the ensemble approach. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a framework to decouple case forecasting from Rt estimation, improving real-time monitoring of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in Hong Kong's Omicron outbreaks. The approach mitigates right-censoring artefacts and supports timely public health decision-making.

title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD–ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD–ACE2 interaction, as the ACE2-binding interface is a critical target for antiviral intervention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using a structure- and affinity-based screening approach, focusing on SARS-CoV-2 and its variants, with an emphasis on the RBD region and its interaction with ACE2.
analysis.methods: Structure-based virtual screening was performed using the SARS-CoV-1 RBD as a structural surrogate, and selected compounds were evaluated using an affinity-based assay on diazirine-modified amorphous carbon plates.
analysis.main_results: Evaluation of 175 virtual hits identified eight RBD-binding compounds, among which RABI-1 inhibited RBD–ACE2 interaction in a Calu-3 cell-based binding assay without affecting ACE2 expression or cell viability. RABI-3, a structural analog of RABI-1, showed stronger inhibitory activity and suppressed pseudovirus infection in Calu-3 cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that targeting conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD is a feasible strategy for developing small-molecule inhibitors of viral entry.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide a foundation for the development of antiviral therapies targeting SARS-CoV-2 entry, which could be relevant for managing COVID-19 and its variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on in vitro assays, which may not fully reflect in vivo efficacy or long-term effects.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD–ACE2 interaction, a critical step in viral entry. Using structure- and affinity-based screening, the researchers evaluated 175 virtual hits and identified eight RBD-binding compounds. Among these, RABI-1 inhibited the RBD–ACE2 interaction in a Calu-3 cell-based assay without affecting ACE2 expression or cell viability. A structural analog, RABI-3, showed stronger inhibitory activity and suppressed pseudovirus infection in Calu-3 cells. The findings support the feasibility of targeting conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD for antiviral development. The study is based on in vitro assays and abstract-only evidence, which may limit its generalizability and confidence in real-world applications.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of COVID-19 in Japan: The twelve epidemic waves from 2020 to 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Since the first confirmed case of COVID-19 in Japan in January 2020, multiple epidemic waves have emerged under changing legal classifications and public health measures. Although nationwide surveillance data have been continuously available, integrated analyses of temporal and geographic patterns remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study described the spatiotemporal evolution of COVID-19 in Japan in relation to the timing of major policy, vaccination, variant, and surveillance changes, using weekly prefecture-level case counts from 2020 to 2025.
analysis.methods: Weekly prefecture-level case counts from 2020 to 2025 were analyzed using official data from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, and the epidemic period was divided into early epidemic, expansion, and plateau phases. Three-dimensional log-transformed visualizations were generated to illustrate nationwide temporal and regional trends.
analysis.main_results: We identified twelve epidemic waves. Early outbreaks were localized in densely populated urban areas with low synchrony. During the expansion phase, large nationwide waves occurred in the period when a highly transmissible variant emerged, and peak timing was most closely aligned across prefectures in the 5th and 7th waves. In the plateau phase, following the transition to “Category 5 infectious disease,” reported waves were lower and more prolonged, with smaller differences among prefectures; because these values are based on sentinel reports, they are not directly comparable with earlier phases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Overall, COVID-19 in Japan evolved from localized clusters to synchronized nationwide waves with reduced regional differences across prefectures, suggesting the value of integrated spatiotemporal surveillance frameworks for future pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that integrated spatiotemporal surveillance is crucial for understanding and managing future pandemic waves, especially as variants and public health measures evolve.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on sentinel reports in the plateau phase, which may not be directly comparable with earlier phases. The analysis does not account for all potential confounding factors, such as non-compliance with public health measures or differences in testing rates.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the spatiotemporal evolution of COVID-19 in Japan from 2020 to 2025, identifying twelve epidemic waves. It highlighted the transition from localized outbreaks to synchronized nationwide waves, emphasizing the importance of integrated surveillance for future pandemic preparedness.

title: Predictors and prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19: a prospective observational study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dysfunctional breathing is increasingly recognised among individuals with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), yet data on long-term prevalence and predictors are scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing, as indicated by elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, four years after COVID-19 illness in adults with PCC and identified associated factors and baseline predictors by comparing individuals with and without elevated NQ scores.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this prospective observational study, adults with PCC, both previously hospitalised and non-hospitalised for COVID-19, were recruited from a specialised post-COVID outpatient clinic. These individuals were younger, often female, and more frequently non-hospitalised during acute COVID-19.
analysis.methods: Baseline assessments (2020-2022) were analysed together with data from a digital follow-up survey in 2024. Between group differences were examined, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors and baseline predictors.
analysis.main_results: Among 288 participants (median follow-up 50 months), 143 (50%) had symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing. Elevated NQ scores (≥ 23) were independently associated with higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing were independently associated with higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, highlighting their potential clinical relevance in long-term PCC.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that dysfunctional breathing symptoms may be a significant aspect of long-term PCC, which could inform future surveillance, diagnosis, and management strategies for individuals with prolonged post-COVID-19 symptoms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and reliance on self-reported outcomes, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single cohort study with no randomised control.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the prevalence and predictors of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19 in adults with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC). It finds that 50% of participants had elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, indicating dysfunctional breathing. These individuals were younger, more frequently non-hospitalised during acute illness, and had higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms, and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. The study highlights the potential clinical relevance of these symptoms in long-term PCC management. However, the observational design and reliance on self-reported data limit the confidence in the findings, resulting in a moderate evidence assessment.

title: Evolution of the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across three COVID-19 waves in Central Kerala: a cross-sectional study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the clinical profile, laboratory findings, cardiac manifestations, treatment patterns and outcomes of children diagnosed with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves of the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in a tertiary care teaching hospital in Central Kerala, India. The study included 95 children fulfilling established diagnostic criteria for MIS-C admitted between November 2020 and December 2022.
analysis.methods: Patients were categorised into three groups according to the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant wave: Alpha (wave 1), Delta (wave 2) and Omicron (wave 3). The main outcome measures included clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, echocardiographic findings, treatment modalities and markers of disease severity.
analysis.main_results: Gastrointestinal symptoms remained the predominant presentation across all three waves, whereas respiratory symptoms increased during the later waves. The duration of hospital stay, duration of fever and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels decreased significantly over successive waves. Pericardial effusion also decreased significantly, while the prevalence of left ventricular dysfunction showed a declining trend. In contrast, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The marked increase in coronary artery dilatation during the Omicron wave highlights the importance of continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up, even during clinically milder phases of the pandemic.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the clear comparison across distinct pandemic waves and the use of established diagnostic criteria.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study compared the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of children with MIS-C across three waves of the COVID-19 pandemic in Central Kerala, India. The study included 95 children diagnosed with MIS-C between November 2020 and December 2022, categorised by the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant: Alpha, Delta, and Omicron. Key findings showed that gastrointestinal symptoms remained the most common presentation, while respiratory symptoms increased in later waves. The study observed a significant decrease in disease severity markers such as hospital stay duration, fever duration, and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels over time. However, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave, indicating persistent cardiac involvement. The authors concluded that the clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across pandemic waves, with reduced systemic disease severity but ongoing changes in cardiac manifestations. These findings underscore the need for continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up for MIS-C patients, even during milder pandemic phases. The study's cross-sectional design and use of established diagnostic criteria provide moderate confidence in its conclusions.

title: Structural insights into subunit exchange inhibition and ligand-induced dimerization of SARS-CoV-2 main protease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the structural dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro) and its response to peptidomimetic inhibitors, which are critical for understanding their therapeutic effects on viral polyprotein processing.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform to analyze the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors, focusing on SARS-CoV-2 and its variants.
analysis.methods: The researchers used metabolic 15 N labeling, native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to examine the structural changes and dimerization dynamics of M pro in response to inhibitors.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that apo-M pro exists in a dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium with rapid subunit exchange, and that peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization and highlight the N-finger region as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, offering new insights into the structural modulation of M pro by therapeutic agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide critical structural insights that can inform the development of more effective antiviral drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2 main protease, with potential implications for improving therapeutic strategies against COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro analyses using mass spectrometry and simulations, and the evidence is based on abstract-level reporting, which may not fully capture in vivo dynamics. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro) and its response to peptidomimetic inhibitors. The research highlights the dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium of apo-M pro and demonstrates that inhibitors like nirmatrelvir can trap the dimeric state, stabilizing it and suppressing subunit exchange. The findings reveal that inhibitor binding induces conformational stabilization beyond the active site, affecting the N-finger and dimer interface. These results offer a mechanistic understanding of how inhibitors modulate M pro dimerization, which has implications for the development of more effective antiviral therapies. However, the study is limited to in vitro analyses and abstract-level reporting, which may not fully reflect in vivo conditions, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Social support networks of older adults before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the social support networks of older adults in Slovenia before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. It examines the prevalence and characteristics of different types of social support networks, including informal support from relatives, friends, and neighbors, and how these networks have evolved over time, particularly in response to the pandemic.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a cross-sectional survey conducted in Slovenia in 2002, 2020, and 2025, collecting ego-centred network data from older adults (65+). The data were analyzed using clustering for symbolic data and correspondence analysis. The samples are representative of both gender and region.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies five distinct types of social support networks: family dependent, private restricted, local self-contained, locally integrated, and wider community network. It also notes the emergence of a group called 'no-listed alters' who reported no informal social support. The prevalence of these network types suggests that some were more affected by the pandemic, while others reflect longer-term demographic changes. By 2025, the share of older adults with no social support had dropped to 4.4%, indicating partial recovery.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Persistent inequalities in social support are observed, with men being more likely to experience social isolation. The review highlights the need for targeted social services to address these disparities. However, the evidence does not provide detailed mechanisms or explanations for these inequalities, nor does it explore the impact of specific SARS-CoV-2 variants on social support networks.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that social services should focus on proactive support for socially isolated older adults, particularly men. Further research is needed to understand the underlying reasons for persistent inequalities and to explore how different SARS-CoV-2 variants may influence social support dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the social support networks of older adults in Slovenia from 2002 to 2025, with a focus on changes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. It identifies five distinct network types and highlights the emergence of a group with no listed social support. While some network types were significantly impacted by the pandemic, others reflect long-term demographic shifts. By 2025, the proportion of older adults with no social support decreased to 4.4%, indicating partial recovery. However, persistent inequalities, particularly among men, suggest the need for targeted interventions. The review underscores the importance of understanding how social support networks evolve in response to public health crises and calls for further research to address disparities and explore the influence of SARS-CoV-2 variants on these networks.

title: Misinformation-based preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar: A cross-sectional study

analysis.scope_and_question: This study aimed to examine associations between misinformation-based preventive behaviors (MPB) and sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media use, and health belief factors in Myanmar.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among adults residing in Myanmar, with data collected between March and May 2024. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire adapted from previous COVID-19 studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Use of social media platforms other than Facebook was associated with higher engagement in MPB (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.30, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.22–4.35). Participants reporting ≤3 hours and 4–6 hours of daily social media use had lower odds of MPB engagement compared with those reporting >6 hours (AOR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25–0.86; AOR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.24–0.95, respectively). Higher self-efficacy was independently associated with greater engagement in MPB (AOR = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.03–2.82). MPB were more strongly associated with information environments and specific health beliefs than with sociodemographic characteristics alone.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence on determinants of misinformation-based preventive behaviors remained limited.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings underscore the importance of addressing misinformation and improving access to reliable health information to reduce engagement in non–evidence-based practices.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in Myanmar investigated the association between misinformation-based preventive behaviors (MPB) and sociodemographic factors, information sources, social media use, and health beliefs. The study found that social media use outside of Facebook was linked to higher MPB engagement, while limited daily social media use was associated with lower engagement. Higher self-efficacy was also independently linked to increased MPB engagement. The research highlights the role of information environments and health beliefs in shaping MPB, suggesting that improving access to reliable health information could help reduce non-evidence-based practices. However, the evidence on the determinants of MPB remains limited, indicating a need for further research.

title: Methods to Account for Competing Events With Unknown Duration in Health Policy Evaluations: The Case of COVID-19.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare methods for estimating policy effects in the presence of competing events such as COVID-19. The background highlights the need for robust analytical approaches to account for competing events with unknown durations in health policy evaluations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A simulation study was conducted to evaluate the performance of single interrupted time series (ITS) and comparative interrupted time series (CITS) estimators when policy implementation occurred near a competing event, specifically COVID-19. The study included 2080 scenarios with varying durations of COVID-19 effects, time between policy implementation and COVID-19 onset, and magnitudes of policy effects.
analysis.methods: The methods involved creating simulated time series with 99 monthly observations from October 2015 to December 2023. Two ITS approaches were tested: one assuming different durations of COVID-19 effects (ITS-Assume) and another using grid search to find the best-fitting duration (ITS-Grid Search). Outcomes measured were percent bias, power, and Type 1 error.
analysis.main_results: CITS had the lowest bias and Type 1 error and maintained high power across scenarios, except for intercept changes and when assumptions about shared COVID-19 effects between treatment and control groups were violated. ITS-Grid Search showed lower bias and Type 1 error than ITS-Assume, which produced biased estimates when assumptions were incorrect.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that estimation approaches leveraging control groups, like CITS, can reduce bias from competing events in ITS frameworks. They noted that ITS-Grid Search outperforms methods assuming a priori durations without requiring a control group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the cautious use of ITS methods in health policy evaluations involving competing events like COVID-19, emphasizing the importance of control groups and adaptive duration estimation to improve accuracy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on simulated data and the assumption that policy effects and competing events can be quantified. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a simulation study without real-world validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates methods for estimating policy effects in the presence of competing events like COVID-19, focusing on interrupted time series (ITS) and comparative ITS (CITS) approaches. It highlights that CITS reduces bias and Type 1 error, while ITS-Grid Search outperforms ITS-Assume in duration estimation. The results suggest that ITS methods should be used cautiously, especially when competing events have unknown durations. The study's findings have implications for improving the accuracy of health policy evaluations during pandemics. However, the reliance on simulated data and assumptions about policy effects limits the strength of the evidence.

title: Epidemiology of influenza before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic in China: An observational study from Zhejiang, China (2010-2023).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate how the Zero-COVID policy in China affected influenza trends, as the epidemiology of influenza has shifted due to social restrictions from the pandemic, and it remains unclear whether these changes apply to China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This observational study analyzed weekly surveillance data from Zhejiang Province, China, spanning 2010-2023, including individual-level data from 24,165 cases between 2017-2023. The study focused on influenza diagnoses during the implementation and relaxation of the Zero-COVID policy.
analysis.methods: The researchers applied changepoint detection to identify structural shifts in influenza trends and used interrupted time-series models to quantify the impact of the policy by comparing predicted (P) and observed (O) cases through differences (O - P) and ratios (P/O). Individual-level data were analyzed for lineage and demographic changes.
analysis.main_results: During the Zero-COVID policy, observed influenza cases dropped by 248,781 in 2020 (P/O: 2.40; 95% prediction interval, 2.28 to 2.52), 204,619 in 2021 (1.72; 1.63 to 1.81), and 199,773 in 2022 (1.66; 1.58 to 1.76). After policy relaxation in 2023, cases exceeded expectations by 148,662 (0.8; 0.76 to 0.84), but declines in children under 5 persisted. The B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic (>99% of cases in 2021), while influenza A/H3 (55%) and A/H1 (41%) became the most prevalent strains by 2023.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets that China's Zero-COVID policy was associated with changes in influenza transmission dynamics, with explosive outbreaks after relaxation except among young children. It highlights the intensification of lineage predominance during and after restrictions, with uncertain long-term implications.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the understanding of how public health policies can influence influenza transmission dynamics and provide insights into the potential for future outbreaks following policy changes, particularly in different age groups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on surveillance data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on observational data and comparisons of predicted versus observed cases.

analysis.summary_en: This observational study from Zhejiang, China, examines how the Zero-COVID policy impacted influenza trends between 2010 and 2023. The researchers used weekly surveillance data and individual-level case data to analyze changes in influenza cases and lineage predominance. They found that during the policy, observed cases dropped significantly in 2020, 2021, and 2022, but increased after relaxation in 2023, with declines in children under 5 persisting. The B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic, while A/H3 and A/H1 strains became more prevalent by 2023. The study suggests that the Zero-COVID policy altered influenza transmission dynamics, with potential long-term implications. However, the evidence is moderate due to reliance on observational data and possible confounding factors.

title: Gender differences regarding body image-related aspects in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review addresses how the COVID-19 pandemic (target disease) has affected body‐image related outcomes in the general adult population, focusing on gender differences in dissatisfaction, shame, and related constructs. Its central question is whether women and men differ in body‐image concerns during the pandemic.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The systematic review was preregistered on PROSPERO (CRD42023421727) and followed PRESS and PRISMA guidelines (A5). Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and PsycINFO for studies published between January 2019 and July 2024 (A6). Inclusion required original studies reporting gender‐specific analyses of body‐image outcomes in non‐clinical adults during COVID‐19 (A7). Sixteen studies with a total of 9,813 participants met the criteria (A10). Study quality was appraised with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist (A8).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across the majority of included studies, women reported higher levels of body dissatisfaction, weight and shape concerns, body shame, guilt, and dysmorphic concerns than men (A11). Men generally showed lower dissatisfaction and higher body satisfaction, often perceiving themselves as slimmer or more athletic (A12). The authors conclude that women generally experienced greater body‐image concerns during the pandemic, despite some inconsistencies (A16).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Three studies found no significant gender differences and one reported higher dissatisfaction among men, indicating heterogeneity in findings (A13). Evidence for sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals remains sparse and under‐represented (A15; A17). Additionally, longitudinal data are limited, with only one study noting increasing dissatisfaction in men over time (A14).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The authors call for further longitudinal and gender‐diverse research to clarify body‐image trajectories during public‐health crises and to guide targeted prevention and intervention strategies (A18).

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examined gender differences in body‐image concerns among adults during the COVID‐19 pandemic. Sixteen studies (9,813 participants) were identified through comprehensive database searches and assessed for quality. The prevailing evidence shows that women experienced greater body dissatisfaction, weight‐shape concerns, and related shame than men, while men reported higher body satisfaction and a slimmer self‐perception. However, a minority of studies reported no gender effect or even higher dissatisfaction in men, and data on sexual and gender minority groups are limited. Longitudinal insights are scarce, with only one report of rising dissatisfaction in men over time. The authors recommend additional longitudinal, gender‐inclusive investigations to better inform prevention and intervention efforts in future public‐health emergencies.

title: Investigation of anti-SARS-CoV-2 multimeric bicyclic peptide inhibitors in a range of preclinical therapeutic settings

analysis.research_question_and_background: The spread of respiratory viruses, such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2, has presented significant challenges over the last 30 years, with few effective therapeutic options available to this day.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study utilizes tool molecules to provide a deeper evaluation of multivalent bicyclic (Bicycle) molecule efficacy in several preclinical SARS-CoV-2 challenge settings.
analysis.methods: We explore both pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure therapeutic settings via subcutaneous and intranasal routes of administration.
analysis.main_results: Promisingly, in all studies, we observe efficacy, significantly reducing infectious viral burden at each study endpoint.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These data further support the candidacy of Bicycle molecules as a differentiated antiviral therapeutic class in the context of pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The Bicycle molecules demonstrated positive outcomes in each of these studies and suggest that Bicycle molecules, as convenient and effective antiviral treatments, could be an important addition to help future preparedness against new viral pandemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the efficacy of multimeric bicyclic peptide inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 in preclinical therapeutic settings. The research aims to evaluate the potential of these molecules as antiviral treatments, focusing on their effectiveness in reducing infectious viral burden through various routes of administration, including subcutaneous and intranasal. The findings suggest that Bicycle molecules show promising results in all tested scenarios, supporting their candidacy as a novel therapeutic class for pandemic preparedness. The study provides insights into the application of these molecules in different contexts, such as compromised immune systems and viral transmission. However, the evidence does not report specific limitations or the strength of the findings. The results highlight the potential of these molecules to contribute to future antiviral strategies against SARS-CoV-2 and related respiratory viruses.

title: From Viral Detection to Disease Measurement: Lessons from COVID-19.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to highlight the distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the disease it produces, as demonstrated by the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a conceptual analysis of the relationship between viral infection and disease, focusing on SARS-CoV-2 and its associated clinical outcomes.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review and synthesis of existing knowledge on viral detection, disease measurement, and the factors influencing their relationship, including viral evolution, immunity, and human behavior.
analysis.main_results: The results emphasize that viral genetic material detection does not equate to quantifying tissue injury, systemic thromboinflammation, or disease severity, and that individual biomarkers reflect components of a biological response rather than the complete disease state.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the pandemic has shown the need to distinguish between infection and disease, and that this distinction is crucial for accurate measurement and understanding of the biological processes involved.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of integrating pathogen detection with appropriate measurements of host response, tissue injury, and clinical outcomes to improve pandemic preparedness and public health responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to conceptual analysis and does not provide empirical data, but it offers a high-level framework for understanding the relationship between infection and disease.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the resulting disease, using the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study. It highlights that viral genetic material detection alone does not quantify disease severity or mechanisms. The authors argue that future pandemic preparedness must integrate pathogen detection with mechanistically appropriate measurements of host response and clinical outcomes. The study provides a conceptual framework for understanding the relationship between infection and disease, emphasizing the need to maintain explicit boundaries between measurement, inference, and causation. While the analysis is abstract-based and lacks empirical data, it offers important insights into improving public health strategies. The evidence is moderate in strength due to its conceptual nature and the absence of direct experimental results.

title: Host-Directed p53 and NRF2 Co-Activation Reverses Acute COVID-19 and Long COVID Pathology by Restoring the miR-29 and miR-145 Epigenetic Axis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of phase-independent mechanistic therapies for COVID-19 and Long COVID by proposing a host-directed therapeutic framework targeting p53 and NRF2 co-activation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis to evaluate the therapeutic potential of co-activating p53 and NRF2 across both acute and post-acute phases of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.methods: The study used stiff ordinary differential equation (ODE) simulations (solve_ivp/BDF) parameterized from published turnover kinetics to model the effects of p53/NRF2 co-activation on miR-29 and miR-145 dynamics and their downstream effectors.
analysis.main_results: Simulations showed that p53/NRF2 co-activation induced a sharp bifurcation switch near an agonist threshold of Uth = 0.4–0.6, resulting in a 13.75-fold recovery of miR-29, a 54.39-fold recovery of miR-145, and a 94.0% suppression of NF-κB, with reductions in IFN-γ, TF, Sema3a, and GzmK by 98.3% to 99.1% in locked PASC steady states.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that co-activating p53 and NRF2 can reverse the pathological effects of SARS-CoV-2 by restoring the miR-29 and miR-145 epigenetic axis, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for both acute and post-acute phases of infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest a potential new approach for treating both acute and long-term sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection, which could inform future research and therapeutic development for COVID-19 and related conditions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis, with key caveats including incomplete extraction of miR-29 viral sites, cross-species differences in miR-145 validation, and the absence of prospective randomized trials, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the lack of phase-independent mechanistic therapies for COVID-19 and Long COVID by proposing a host-directed therapeutic framework centered on co-activating p53 and NRF2. Using in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis, the authors demonstrate that co-activating these stress-response regulators can restore the miR-29 and miR-145 epigenetic axis, reversing the pathological effects of SARS-CoV-2. The simulations show significant recovery of miR-29 and miR-145 and suppression of key inflammatory effectors in locked PASC steady states. However, the study's reliance on computational models and absence of prospective randomized trials limit the confidence in its findings, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

title: Intranasal azelastine for the treatment and prevention of SARS-CoV-2: A systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of randomized trials

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examined the efficacy and safety of intranasal azelastine for treating established SARS‐CoV‐2 infection and preventing incident infection, focusing on virological outcomes, prevention efficacy, and safety in randomized trials.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library through January 16, 2026 identified randomized controlled trials comparing intranasal azelastine to placebo; risk of bias was assessed with RoB‐2 and certainty with GRADE, and random‐effects meta‐analysis was employed where appropriate.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Moderate‐certainty evidence indicated a greater reduction in SARS‐CoV‐2 viral load at day 3 with intranasal azelastine in established infection, though the clinical relevance of this surrogate outcome remains uncertain.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence for prevention was limited to a single randomized trial, and safety findings varied between treatment and prevention populations, underscoring the exploratory nature of the data.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The current evidence is insufficient to confirm clinical benefit on patient‐important outcomes, highlighting the need for larger, well‐designed trials to clarify efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and exploratory meta‐analysis evaluated intranasal azelastine for treating and preventing SARS‐CoV‐2 infection. Searches of major databases up to January 2026 yielded three randomized controlled trials (754 participants). Meta‐analysis showed a modest, statistically significant reduction in viral load at day 3 in treatment trials, but the effect waned by day 5/6 and was not significant by day 11. A single prevention trial suggested a 67 % relative risk reduction in PCR‐confirmed infection, yet safety outcomes differed between treatment and prevention groups. Overall, moderate‐certainty evidence points to an early virological benefit, yet the clinical relevance is unclear, and the limited number of trials and heterogeneous safety data preclude definitive conclusions. Further large, rigorously designed studies are required to determine whether intranasal azelastine offers meaningful patient‐important benefits.

title: Comparison of methodological approaches in COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness estimation using observational data

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare different methodological approaches for estimating vaccine effectiveness (VE) against SARS-CoV-2 infection using observational data, addressing the challenge of design-related biases in causal inference.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used observational data from an ongoing prospective cohort study in the Netherlands, estimating VE of the Omicron XBB.1.5 booster vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 infection between 2 October 2023 and 2 April 2024.
analysis.methods: A hypothetical target trial was designed where participants were randomly assigned to receive booster vaccination or not, and four approaches were used to emulate this trial using the cohort data.
analysis.main_results: Overall VE was 30% (95%CI:26-34), 28% (24-32), 25% (18-30) and 27% (24-31) in the first, second, third and fourth approach, respectively. VE decreased as time since vaccination increased.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the estimated VE was similar across the four approaches, highlighting the importance of selecting an approach based on model assumptions, estimand of interest, and feasibility.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the choice of methodological approaches for estimating vaccine effectiveness in observational studies, which is critical for public health decision-making and vaccine policy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the estimated VE values are based on hypothetical trial emulation, which may not fully capture real-world complexities. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares four methodological approaches for estimating vaccine effectiveness (VE) of the Omicron XBB.1.5 booster against SARS-CoV-2 infection using observational data from a Dutch cohort. The approaches included regression adjustment, inverse probability weighting, and varying definitions of time zero. Overall VE estimates ranged from 25% to 30%, with a decline over time since vaccination. The authors concluded that VE estimates were similar across methods, emphasizing the need to select approaches based on model assumptions and feasibility. The study's findings have implications for improving VE estimation in observational studies, which is important for public health decision-making. However, the evidence is based solely on abstract data, limiting the confidence in the results to a moderate level.

title: Detection of SARS-CoV-2 in Semen Months After COVID-19: Potential Evidence of Low-Level Replicative Persistence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The male genital tract (MGT), particularly the testis, is an immune-privileged site that may serve as a viral reservoir for SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: MATERIAL AND METHODS: This observational, prospective, cross-sectional study included 38 men treated at Mater Dei Hospital, Brazil, between October 2020 and October 2021, who had recovered from mild to moderate COVID-19 and consented to participate.
analysis.methods: Semen samples were collected from mildly symptomatic participants at approximately 1 month (15- 45 days), 3 months, and 6 months after symptom onset.
analysis.main_results: SARS-CoV-2 was detected by RT-qPCR in 21 of 38 patients (55%), with high cycle threshold (Ct 38-39) values observed for more than 6 months post-infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that the MGT may serve as a viral reservoir, highlighting the importance of longitudinal semen analysis for monitoring viral persistence and reservoir dynamics after clinical recovery.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study provides evidence of the long-term persistence of viral RNA and culture-derived signals suggestive of restricted or low-level replicative activity in semen.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This deterministic extraction is based on abstract only. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

analysis.summary_en: The male genital tract (MGT), particularly the testis, is an immune-privileged site that may serve as a viral reservoir for SARS-CoV-2. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This observational, prospective, cross-sectional study included 38 men treated at Mater Dei Hospital, Brazil, between October 2020 and October 2021, who had recovered from mild to moderate COVID-19 and consented to participate. Semen samples were collected from mildly symptomatic participants at approximately 1 month (15- 45 days), 3 months, and 6 months after symptom onset. SARS-CoV-2 was detected by RT-qPCR in 21 of 38 patients (55%), with high cycle threshold (Ct 38-39) values observed for more than 6 months post-infection. These findings suggest that the MGT may serve as a viral reservoir, highlighting the importance of longitudinal semen analysis for monitoring viral persistence and reservoir dynamics after clinical recovery. This study provides evidence of the long-term persistence of viral RNA and culture-derived signals suggestive of restricted or low-level replicative activity in semen. This deterministic extraction is based on abstract only. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

title: Glycoform Distributions and Heparan Sulfate Binding of Intact SARS-CoV-2 Spike Variants by DIA-ECCR Native Mass Spectrometry

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenges in characterizing the extensive heterogeneity of glycoform distributions in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, which has hindered understanding of its structure, immunogenicity, and evolutionary selection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research introduced a data-independent analysis - electron capture charge reduction (DIA-ECCR) native mass spectrometry workflow to directly analyze intact spike glycoforms across multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.methods: The study utilized DIA-ECCR native mass spectrometry to resolve variant-dependent differences in glycoform distributions and higher mass subpopulations, with Monte Carlo simulations based on site-specific bottom-up glycoproteomic data used to support the findings.
analysis.main_results: Monte Carlo simulations reproduced the central mass of the D614G experimental distribution and supported a connection between intact and bottom-up measurements, while broader experimental distributions and a second Gamma subpopulation indicated heterogeneity not captured by the simulations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate the utility of DIA-ECCR in analyzing heterogeneous protein:ligand complexes, such as those formed with truncated heparan sulfate, and outline a practical workflow for characterizing glycoform distributions and ligand binding.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings have potential applications in antigen characterization, vaccine design, and biopharmaceutical quality control, offering insights into the structural and functional diversity of SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that Monte Carlo simulations may not fully capture the heterogeneity observed in experimental distributions, suggesting that further validation with additional methods is needed to strengthen the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of characterizing the extensive heterogeneity of glycoform distributions in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, which has hindered understanding of its structure and immunogenicity. The research introduces a data-independent analysis - electron capture charge reduction (DIA-ECCR) native mass spectrometry workflow to directly analyze intact spike glycoforms across multiple variants. The methods employed include DIA-ECCR and Monte Carlo simulations based on site-specific bottom-up glycoproteomic data. The main results show that while simulations reproduce the central mass of the D614G experimental distribution, broader experimental distributions and a second Gamma subpopulation indicate heterogeneity not captured by the simulations. The study also demonstrates the analysis of a heterogeneous protein:ligand complex formed with truncated heparan sulfate. These findings outline a practical workflow for characterizing glycoform distributions and ligand binding, with potential applications in vaccine design and biopharmaceutical quality control. The study notes that Monte Carlo simulations may not fully capture the observed heterogeneity, highlighting the need for further validation with additional methods.

title: Post-COVID-19 Emergence and Spread of Hypertransmissible Cryptosporidium hominis gp60 Subtype IfA12G1R5, Spain.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how the COVID-19 pandemic affected the transmission dynamics of Cryptosporidium hominis in Spain, particularly focusing on the emergence of hypertransmissible gp60 subtypes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed Cryptosporidium hominis transmission patterns in Spain during and after the 2020 pandemic, noting the rapid emergence and spread of hypertransmissible subtypes such as IfA12G1R5.
analysis.methods: The study examined the impact of pandemic containment measures on Cryptosporidium hominis transmission, highlighting how these measures selectively altered anthroponotic transmission and led to the emergence of hypertransmissible subtypes.
analysis.main_results: The study observed that the emergence and spread of hypertransmissible human-adapted gp60 subtypes, such as IfA12G1R5, were more pronounced compared to the relatively stable transmission of the largely zoonotic C.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of pandemic containment measures influencing the transmission dynamics of Cryptosporidium hominis, leading to the dominance of hypertransmissible subtypes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that pandemic-related public health interventions may have indirectly influenced the epidemiology of Cryptosporidium hominis, with implications for surveillance and understanding of anthroponotic transmission patterns.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis and the confidence in its conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the impact of the 2020 pandemic containment measures on the transmission dynamics of Cryptosporidium hominis in Spain. It highlights the emergence and spread of hypertransmissible gp60 subtypes, such as IfA12G1R5, as a result of these measures, while noting that the largely zoonotic C. parvum transmission remained stable. The authors interpret this as evidence of pandemic interventions altering anthroponotic transmission patterns. The findings suggest potential implications for surveillance and understanding of Cryptosporidium hominis epidemiology. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the confidence in its conclusions. The research contributes to understanding how public health measures can influence the spread of non-SARS-CoV-2 pathogens, offering insights into the interplay between pandemic responses and other infectious diseases.
